classification.difficultyReason: A qualitative representation change. The student reads the turning points and concavity changes off an unscaled quartic and converts them into the zeros and sign pattern of $f'$. Then they convert the turning points of $f'$ into the zeros of $f''$. It needs no calculus computation but requires coordinating the three graphs. Two sketches are required and the scale is imprecise.

content.prompt: By considering the sign of the graph, sketch $f'(x)$ and then sketch $f''(x)$.

answer.short: $f'$ is a cubic shape with three $x$-intercepts below the turning points of $f$: negative, positive, negative, positive. $f''$ is an upward-opening parabola with its two zeros below the turning points of $f'$.
answer.worked:
$f$ decreases, then increases, then decreases, then increases, so $f'$ is negative, positive, negative, positive. Its three zeros are directly beneath the minimum, maximum and minimum of $f$. Draw a cubic shape through these zeros, rising from bottom left to top right.

The graph of $f'$ has a maximum and then a minimum between these zeros. Beneath these points $f''=0$. So $f''$ is positive, negative, positive: $f$ is concave up, then concave down, then concave up. Draw an upward-opening parabola with these two zeros.
